core_obligations: Reduce to the case where S and Y are affine, the question being local on both (proof lines 4621-4622).
Use openness of f and quasi-compactness of Y to find finitely many affine opens X_i of X covering Y, and replace X by their disjoint union (proof lines 4622-4628).
Identify the resulting affine situation with the algebra permanence lemma (resp. the finite type version) and conclude (proof lines 4629-4632).
proof_roadmap: Localisation to affine S and Y (proof lines 4621-4622).
Openness of f and reduction to X affine (proof lines 4622-4628).
Identification with the algebra statement (proof lines 4629-4632).
difficulty_reason: In the commutative triangle with f : X -> Y surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation and p : X -> S locally of finite presentation (resp. locally of finite type), the lemma concludes the same finiteness property for q : Y -> S (statement lines 4601-4618). The proof is a genuine reduction: the question is local on S and Y, so both may be taken affine; flat local finite presentation makes f open, so finitely many affine opens X_i of X cover Y, and replacing X by their disjoint union reduces to X affine; in that case the statement is exactly the algebra lemma for flat finitely presented permanence (resp. the algebra lemma for finite type on the source) (proof lines 4620-4632). The level is H3: the reduction runs through openness of f and a finiteness argument on the covering, and both the reduction and the final identification with the algebra statement are displayed.
